claims.text: Realistically processed bulk HfNbTaTiZr contains inherent defects, including approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed supervised regression model is trained using DFT-based defect simulations, mesoscale transport simulations, and experimental conductivity data from oxygen-containing specimens.
Combining physics-based calculations with data-driven methods is an established strategy for advanced HEA prediction.
Oxygen-related defects act as electron-scattering centers in HfNbTaTiZr.
Phonon interactions alter electron transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
The combined defect and phonon scattering processes produce nonlinear temperature dependence in conductivity.
Conventional analytical conductivity models assume perfect, defect-free crystalline order.
Perfect-crystal analytical models do not capture oxygen-induced and other defect-induced scattering in processed HfNbTaTiZr.
Training on realistic defect simulations and corresponding experiments allows the ML model to learn the interplay between defects and temperature-dependent scattering.
Accounting for realistic defects and nonlinear temperature effects will make the ML model more accurate than conventional analytical models.
Computational predictions for HEAs can disagree with experimental observations and require additional validation.
Existing analytical models have larger conductivity errors for defect-containing or oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr than the proposed ML model.
The model will improve conductivity-prediction accuracy by roughly 20–30% relative to conventional methods.
The accuracy advantage will hold in both the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
The model is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr having processing-typical defects and no more than 1 wt.% oxygen.
Improved accuracy is not claimed outside 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Prediction improvement depends on the quality and representativeness of the training data.
Unmodeled microstructural complexities may reduce the ML model's accuracy advantage.
Conductivity at held-out temperatures such as 150 K and 500 K can benchmark the ML model against conventional models.
Failure to achieve at least a 20% error reduction across both temperature regimes falsifies the hypothesis.
